LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 4.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Months of the Year Suggested vocabulary later, before, after, sunrise, daylight,
Topic 4.1: Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Months of the Year Suggested vocabulary later, before, after, sunrise, daylight, in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we pronounce words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. pronounce words with the target letter- sound combinations as modeled by the teacher or peers, o / ŋ / ing as in thing;/ ŋ o / iː/ as in happy in words ending with letter y o st as in stick o gl as in glass. o

2. say tongue twisters/poems/songs containing the target letter-sound combinations, with peers.

3. pronounce the words related to the theme accurately.

4. construct simple sentences orally using the new words, with peers and give feedback.

5. make a talking tree using the new words related to the theme.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. pronounce words with the target letter- sound combinations as modeled by the teacher or peers, o / ŋ / ing as in thing;/ ŋ o / iː/ as in happy in words ending with letter y o st as in stick o gl as in glass. o
2. say tongue twisters/poems/songs containing the target letter-sound combinations, with peers.
3. pronounce the words related to the theme accurately.
4. construct simple sentences orally using the new words, with peers and give feedback.
5. make a talking tree using the new words related to the theme.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration; the learner’s ability to listen keenly is enhanced as they listen to the teacher/peer model of pronunciation of words

and pronounce the words correctly.

Values:
Unity; the learner’s ability to work collaboratively with others is enhanced as they sing song /recite rhymes to practice pronunciation.

21

Pertinent Contemporary Issues:

Life skill (self-esteem); the learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as they are able to successfully make a talking tree using the new words related to the

theme.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Listening attentively and accurately in pronunciation are emphasized in all learning areas.
